doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Sinatra, Shirley Horn and film songs
title: Writing for voices in films
summary: Mandel says he learned vocal writing by doing it and uses chorus only for a nationality or period, since voices pull the ear from dialogue.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: How did you learn to write for voices? We didn’t talk about that at all.
I never did, I just started doing it. I’d look at – I’d listen to what other people did with voices and figure that out and just started writing myself.
Any vocal writing that in particular influenced you that you can think of?

No. No. I don’t have a very strong vocal style. I just write chorally like Mancini did and in the case of, The Verdict say, or… I went with the genre whichever you do, I was there I was writing almost Gregorian chants in a lot of cases. And in the case of like, The Russians are Coming, I was writing very modal and very Russian type of music. You know you go with what – there’s a reason for using voices to start with, you’re generally either dealing with a nationality or a period because I don’t believe in using voices in movies I think they’re death because there’s nothing that will eat up dialogue faster and pull your ear away from dialogue.
Very, there’s nothing as stirring or powerful in pulling your ear as the human voice. People just start listening to it, whether they want to or not. So…
